subject: Ops visibility: annual slab swap proposal for tracing/retention/dashboards
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@atlashealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasHealth Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>, Sara Cho <sara.cho@atlashealth.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Inquiry: switch to annual slab for observability add-ons

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this. We're looking at consolidating billing and would like to move our observability add-ons (retention, tracing, advanced dashboards) from monthly metered to an annual slab commitment starting Q2.

Current monthly baseline (avg last 6 months):
- Retention: 52 TB/month
- Tracing: ~210M spans/month
- Advanced dashboards: 42 active dashboards (mix of company and team-level)

Procurement asked whether Redwood can:
1) Provide an annual slab SKU (flat monthly equivalent) that smooths spikes and avoids overages;
2) Offer a one-time onboarding credit or first-quarter consumption credit in exchange for an annual commit;
3) Clarify seat/visualization surcharges — can those be waived or rolled into the slab?

I've attached a short request doc (AtlasHealth_Slab_Swap_Request_2027.pdf). Can you share a preliminary price model and any prerequisites (MOU/PO schedule) we should prepare?

Looking for a fast turn — procurement needs a draft by next week.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
VP Engineering, AtlasHealth
liam@atlashealth.com

Attachment: AtlasHealth_Slab_Swap_Request_2027.pdf (stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Feb 2027 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Inquiry: switch to annual slab for observability add-ons

Hi Liam — appreciate the detail and the timeline.

Short answer: yes, we can structure an annual slab that covers retention, tracing ingest, and advanced dashboards. Below is a preliminary framing to get the conversation started — I'll mark internal folks to confirm final concession levels.

Proposed options (all annual commitments, billed monthly as EOM invoices):
A) Base 12-month slab (conservative)
- Retention slab: 600 TB/year (50 TB/mo baseline) — equivalent EOM unit price = $X per TB
- Tracing slab: 2.4B spans/year (200M/mo) — equivalent price = $Y per M spans
- Dashboards: up to 50 dashboards included
- Discount: 12% off list for dashboards; 15% off tracing/retention list price
- Onboarding credit: one-time $25k credit applied to first invoice

B) Commit + smoothing (preferred) — 18-month favorable pricing
- Slightly higher commitment flexibility for seasonal spikes
- Discount: 20% tracing/retention, 18% dashboards
- Waive seat/visualization surcharge for included dashboards
- First-quarter consumption credit: $40k

C) Metered with volume caps (no commit)
- Standard metered rates, overage protections, no credits

Ask: which option maps closest to AtlasHealth's buying preference? If you like B, we'll need a signed MOA (provisionally attached) and a PO schedule.

I've attached a proposed price workbook (Proposed_Annual_Slab_Pricing.xlsx) with line-item math. Karthik/Markus — can you confirm if finance/legal are OK with the B-level concessions (waive seat surcharge + $40k credit) or whether we need to keep the concession lighter?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

---
Attachment: Proposed_Annual_Slab_Pricing.xlsx (stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Feb 2027 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Inquiry: switch to annual slab for observability add-ons

Naomi — quick internal take.

I like framing B as the customer-facing target, but recommend dialing the public-facing numbers slightly back to protect gross margin. Proposed internal counter:
- Offer 18-month commit with a stepped discount: 15% dashboards / 20% tracing&retention once 12-month consumption thresholds are met.
- Provide $30k onboarding credit (instead of $40k) tied to signed MOA within 10 business days.
- Waive seat surcharge for the first 12 months only, revert thereafter unless usage justifies continuing.

If AtlasHealth accepts the stepped structure we can push the larger credit conditional on an invoice schedule and PO. Finance wants the MOA to include an early termination pro-rata clause and a minimum invoice cadence (monthly or quarterly).

Link to pricing playbook for reference: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PRIC-879

-Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Naomi / Karthik — reviewed. I can approve a B-style concession with the following guardrails:
1) 18-month term at 20% off tracing/retention list once committed volumes meet the 12-month baseline;
2) Dashboards at 12% off list (not 18) unless AtlasHealth commits to a renewal uplift guarantee;
3) Seat/visualization surcharge waiver for first 12 months only;
4) Finance must sign off on invoice cadence and early termination pro-rata.

Ask Naomi: present the above as our "commercially approved" starting point. If they accept, legal will draft the MOA with the pro-rata termination clause.

-Markus
VP, Commercial Strategy
markus_klein@redwood.com

- Can the dashboard discount be 15% (midpoint between your original and Markus's note)?
- PO schedule: procurement wants quarterly invoices (Q1 prorated) and a standard 30-day payment term.
- Can you include a clause that preserves data egress rates for the first 12 months?

If you send a redline or MOA with those items I can run it through procurement. We can then push DocuSign as soon as legal greenlights.

If possible we'd like the MOA and provisional invoice schedule in the next 48 hours.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this done.
